subject: Taxes
title: Religion and Tax Compliance
description: One-minute skill: Religion and Tax Compliance.

hook.text: Research shows that religious people are slightly more tax-compliant.

buildup.text: Islam's zakat is a mandatory 2.5% wealth tax, built into faith itself.

discovery.text: Christian tithing culture in the US correlates with higher voluntary compliance.

twist.text: But in countries where churches are tax-exempt and clergy avoid taxes, religious compliance effects disappear.

climax.text: Religion can boost tax morale when it practices what it preaches.

punchline.text: Faith increases compliance—only if the institution pays too.

quiz.question: Under what condition does religion boost tax compliance?
options: When the religious institution also pays taxes and emphasizes community duty
